responsibility: Implements the main Blackfin GCC backend logic in C++, tying the target into GCC’s RTL expansion, calling convention, PIC/FDPIC addressing, frame layout, builtin expansion, assembly printing, scheduling/reorg, hardware-loop handling, and target hook registration. This file owns the executable semantics behind the port’s macros and .md patterns: it maintains per-function machine state, decides register usage and ABI details, expands calls/moves/memcpy and builtins, emits prologues and epilogues, handles Blackfin-specific addressing and workaround behavior, and publishes the targetm hook table for the entire processor family.
same_name_distinction: This is the executable implementation file for the Blackfin port: it contains the C++ logic behind target hooks, ABI decisions, PIC/FDPIC address legalization, prologue/epilogue generation, builtin expansion, and final targetm registration. Unlike bfin.h it does not declare compile-time target macros/interfaces, unlike bfin.md it does not define RTL instruction patterns or scheduling automata, and unlike bfin.opt it does not declare user-visible -m options.
